example_sentences: We pour maple syrup on our pancakes on Sunday mornings.
Real maple syrup costs more than table syrup because it is boiled down from tree sap in Quebec and Ontario sugar bushes.
She ordered poutine at the hockey arena canteen.
Poutine is fries topped with cheese curds and hot gravy — every diner claims its own version is the real one.

translations.hi: पैक कराकर ले जाने वाला खाना

example_sentences: Let's just get takeout tonight, I'm too tired to cook.
Canadians say takeout while Americans say takeaway or to-go — the menu board will say Take-Out.
There are leftovers in the fridge if you get hungry.
After a big holiday dinner, Canadians eat turkey leftovers for days — sandwiches, soup, everything.
The portions at this diner are huge.
Restaurant portions in North America are bigger than many visitors expect, so sharing one plate is normal.
Could I have a few extra napkins, please?
Fast-food counters hand out napkins freely — just ask for a handful when you grab your tray.
We shared an appetizer before the main course.
Appetizers are smaller and cheaper than mains, so two appetizers plus dessert is a perfectly normal dinner order.
Save room for dessert — the carrot cake here is famous.
Don't mix up dessert with desert; one is cake and pie, the other is sand as far as the eye can see.
Beverages are refillable with the combo meal.
On invitations, BYOB means bring your own beverage — checking what it stands for saves awkward moments.

translations.zh: 黄油挞（加拿大传统甜点）

example_sentences: A butter tart is the sweetest thing on the bakery shelf.
Butter tarts are a genuinely Canadian invention — gooey sugar filling in pastry, sometimes with raisins, never with nuts if you're a purist.
The cashier asked if I wanted a bag.
Self-checkout machines still need one cashier watching six lanes, which is why someone always comes over to help.
The price tag never includes sales tax.
Sales tax gets added at the register and varies by province — budget roughly thirteen percent extra in Ontario.
Check the price tag before you get to the till.
If an item scans higher than its price tag, many stores honour the tag — it pays to notice.

translations.hi: बाद में उसी दाम पर खरीदने की पर्ची

example_sentences: They were out of the sale coffee, so I got a rain check.
A rain check is the store's written promise to sell you the sale price when stock arrives — just ask at customer service.
Scan your loyalty card and the points add up fast.
Canadian grocery loyalty programs convert points into free groceries, and stacking them with flyer sales is how careful shoppers save hundreds.
My aunt gave me a gift card for my birthday.
Gift cards are the default Canadian present when you don't know someone's size or taste — check the balance online before shopping.
I clipped a coupon for dish soap from the weekend paper.
Most coupons went digital — load them onto the store app and they apply automatically at checkout.
Winter coats hit clearance in February.
Clearance items are final-sale more often than regular items, so check the return policy before buying.

translations.pa: ਸਟੋਰ ਦਾ ਗਲਿਆਰਾ (ਕਤਾਰ ਦੇ ਵਿਚਕਾਰ ਰਾਹ)

example_sentences: Spices are in aisle seven, next to the baking supplies.
The s in aisle is silent — it sounds exactly like 'I'll', which confuses everyone the first time an announcement says aisle five.
Ask about the return policy before you buy electronics.
Every store sets its own return policy — thirty days with a receipt is common, but final-sale and clearance items often can't come back.
I get to work by transit, door to door in forty minutes.
Each city runs its own transit system — TTC in Toronto, TransLink in Vancouver — each with its own fare cards and apps.
The bus stop outside our building has a shelter and a schedule pole.
Wave at the driver at your bus stop or they may sail past — and pull the cord a block early to request your own stop.
The bus fare went up by ten cents this January.
Fare and fair sound identical — one is what you pay to ride, the other means just or a carnival.
Press the button and wait for the walk signal at the crosswalk.
Cars must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, but making eye contact with the driver first is still the smart move.
Downtown streets close to cars and open for pedestrians all summer.
Pedestrian means a person walking — drivers yield to pedestrians at marked crossings whether or not the light has changed.
Leave before rush hour or the drive doubles to an hour.
Rush hour runs roughly seven to nine in the morning and four to six at night — buses and trains are packed but still faster than driving.
Three of us carpool to the plant and split the gas.
Some highways have diamond-marked carpool lanes that let vehicles with two or more people skip the worst of the jam.
The city snowplow came through at four in the morning and buried the driveway again.
When a snowplow is announced, move your car off the street or risk a ticket — and never try to pass one.
Book your winter tires swap before the first snowfall hits.
Quebec makes winter tires mandatory from December to March, and most insurers elsewhere offer a small discount for using them.
A gravel truck cracked our windshield on the highway.
Gravel cracks and winter frost make windshield chips a rite of passage for Canadian drivers — small ones get repaired free by many insurers.
Schools closed today because of the blizzard warning.
A blizzard means heavy snow plus strong wind plus near-zero visibility — the news names winter storms the way hurricanes get names.
Just flurries today, nothing that sticks.
Flurries mean light scattered snow that melts on contact — the forecast word that promises drama-free driving.
March sidewalks are pure slush — wear the waterproof boots.
Slush is half-melted snow that soaks shoes in seconds, which is why locals switch boots the moment temperatures climb above zero.
Scrape the frost off the windshield before you drive.
The first frost usually lands in October and kills the garden — it also means the car needs five extra minutes every morning.
Summer humidity makes thirty degrees feel like forty.
Weather reports mention the humidex in summer — humidity plus heat measured together — the way winter reports use wind chill.
The city opens cooling centres during a heat wave.
Heat waves are taken seriously — community centres open as cooling centres and news anchors remind you to check on elderly neighbours.
A chinook melted all the snow overnight in Calgary.
The chinook is Alberta's famous warm winter wind that can raise temperatures twenty degrees in an hour and gives Calgarians snow-free Januaries.
In Winnipeg you need a real parka by November.
A true Canadian parka is rated for minus-thirty — the first deep-cold day teaches newcomers why locals spend real money on one coat.
Kids lose mittens constantly — label them with a marker.
Mittens keep hands warmer than gloves because fingers share heat, which is why every schoolyard in January is full of them.
The whole family goes tobogganing after a big snowfall.
Tobogganing is the classic free Canadian winter outing — find a local hill, and some cities ban plastic carpets for safety, so check signs.
They bought a two-bedroom condo downtown last spring.
Condo owners pay monthly maintenance fees covering building upkeep — renters hear the word used loosely for any high-rise apartment.
Townhouse complexes share walls but each unit has its own front door.
Townhouses sit between condos and detached houses — usually three floors, often with a tiny yard and a monthly strata or condo fee.
We store the suitcases in the basement.
Basement apartments are a classic affordable first home for newcomers — cooler in summer, dimmer in winter, and priced accordingly.
The furnace kicked in for the first time this fall.
Most Canadian houses heat with a gas furnace — replace its filter every few months and it quietly earns its keep all winter.
Old houses skimp on insulation, so the bills run high.
Good insulation is invisible but decisive in Canada — rebate programs exist precisely because better insulation cuts heating bills all winter.
The smoke alarm chirps when its battery dies — annoying but lifesaving.
Landlords must keep working smoke alarms in every bedroom level by law, and tenants test them monthly in most provinces.
Sunday morning is quiet in the laundry room.
Shared laundry rooms run on coins or a loaded card — keep loonies handy and set a phone timer so nobody moves your wet towels.
We rented a moving truck for the drive from Montreal.
July first is moving day in Quebec and trucks vanish weeks ahead — book any moving truck early at month-end everywhere in Canada.

translations.pa: ਘਰ ਦੇ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਗੱਡੀ ਦਾ ਰਾਹ
translations.hi: घर के सामने गाड़ी रखने की जगह

example_sentences: Shovelling the driveway after a storm takes an hour.
Driveway culture is real: clearing your driveway promptly is neighbourly, and parking on the street overnight often needs a permit.
The kids were playing tag on the front lawn.
Many cities have lawn-watering rules in dry summers, and letting grass grow past a certain height can earn a bylaw letter.
I see the dentist every nine months for a cleaning.
Adult dental care isn't covered by provincial plans, so many employers' benefit packages list exactly how much the dentist will reimburse.
No cavities this time — keep up the flossing.
A cavity is a little hole of tooth decay; catching it early means a quick filling instead of a root canal later.
The dentist took an X-ray of my back molar.
Capitalize X-ray properly and note it works as noun and verb — they X-rayed my wrist at the urgent care centre.
Schools ask for your child's immunization record at registration.
Immunization is the formal word for getting vaccinated — public health keeps the official record, and schools review it at enrollment.
Two paramedics arrived within six minutes of the 911 call.
Paramedics staff ambulances and bill separately from hospitals in most provinces — knowing their scope helps you answer their questions fast.
Call an ambulance if the chest pain doesn't stop.
Ambulance rides usually carry a provincial fee unless admitted or covered by benefits — a detail worth knowing before you need one.
A sprained wrist belongs at urgent care, not the emergency room.
Urgent care centres handle serious-but-not-life-threatening problems with shorter waits than emergency rooms — pick the right door and save hours.

translations.pa: ਅੱਖਾਂ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਡਾਕਟਰ

example_sentences: Book the optometrist yearly once you hit forty.
Optometrists test vision and prescribe glasses — provinces cover children's and seniors' exams, working-age adults usually pay out of pocket or through benefits.

translations.hi: डेंटल हाइजीनिस्ट (दांत साफ करने वाला विशेषज्ञ)

example_sentences: The dental hygienist does the cleaning before the dentist looks.
You spend more time with the hygienist than the dentist at checkups — they scrape, polish, and teach flossing without judgment.
Put a bandage on the cut and keep it dry today.
Bandage works as noun and verb, and the little sticky strips are also called Band-Aids after the brand, like Kleenex for tissues.
I arranged a shift trade so I could attend the wedding.
Shift trades usually need supervisor approval even when coworkers agree — post it on the break-room board or the scheduling app.
Your lunch is in the break room fridge, third shelf.
Break-room etiquette matters: label your food, wipe the microwave, and the communal coffee pot runs on goodwill.
I'm taking time off in July for my brother's graduation.
Time off splits into paid vacation, unpaid leave, and statutory days — track your banked hours before requesting anything long.
Family Day in February is a statutory holiday in several provinces.
Statutory holidays entitle most employees to the day off with pay, or premium pay like time-and-a-half if they work — rules vary by province.
Minimum wage rises every October in this province.
Minimum wage differs by province and sometimes by role — students serving liquor, for instance, can have their own lower rate in some places.
The dress code is business casual except on Fridays.
When unsure about a dress code, overdress slightly on day one and adjust tomorrow — nobody remembers the person who looked sharp.
My first three months are probation, then benefits kick in.
Probation periods commonly run three months, when both sides decide fit — benefits and sometimes job protections start after it ends.
My volunteer coordinator wrote me a reference letter for the pharmacy job.
Newcomers often build their first Canadian reference letter through volunteering — twenty hours of showing up reliably is usually enough to ask.
The plant announced a layoff of sixty workers until spring.
A layoff is not a firing for cause — seasonal layoffs end with recall, and record-of-employment paperwork unlocks employment insurance.
Payroll arrives by direct deposit every second Thursday.
Set up direct deposit with a void cheque or banking details form — it's how virtually every Canadian employer pays.
The fall semester starts the day after Labour Day.
Colleges run fall and winter semesters plus a compressed summer term — course registration for each opens well before it begins.
College tuition is due in full before classes begin.
Domestic tuition is far lower than international tuition, and payment plans plus tax credits soften the sticker shock.
She won an entrance scholarship for her high-school marks.
Scholarships reward grades or achievements and don't need repaying — many go unclaimed simply because nobody applied.
Universities abroad want an official transcript mailed in a sealed envelope.
A transcript lists every course and grade — credential assessment services use your foreign transcript to equate it with Canadian levels.
Credential recognition took eight months for her nursing degree.
Getting foreign credentials recognized involves assessment agencies and sometimes bridging programs — start the process before you arrive if you can.
He finished his electrician apprenticeship in four years.
Trades training runs on apprenticeships — paid work hours plus classroom blocks — leading to a red seal exam recognized across provinces.
Continuing education courses run evenings at the college for working adults.
Continuing education departments sell short certificates in everything from accounting software to welding — perfect for career changers.
The yellow school bus stops at the corner at 8:05 sharp.
It is illegal to pass a school bus with flashing red lights in either direction — the stop arm means every lane stops.
Perfect attendance earned him a certificate at assembly.
Attendance calls go out automatically when a child is absent — parents phone the office before the bell or expect a callback.
Report cards go home three times a year.
Report cards pair letter grades with teacher comments, and signing the envelope back counts as much as the marks inside.
Mark one circle on the ballot and feed it into the box.
Canada votes on paper ballots counted by hand at each polling place, with scrutineers from each party watching every step.
Our polling station is the school gym two blocks away.
Your assigned polling station prints on the voter information card — vote there on election day, or at any advance poll earlier.
File your tax return by April thirtieth to avoid interest.
A tax return is the annual filing; the refund is what comes back — filing even with no income unlocks quarterly credits.
Keep the notice of assessment — landlords and schools sometimes ask for it.
The notice of assessment arrives weeks after filing as the official receipt of your return; it's proof of income for many applications.
Apply for the child benefit as soon as the baby is registered.
The Canada Child Benefit pays monthly per child based on income — applying happens alongside birth registration or on arrival.
I got a jury duty summons in the mail last month.
Jury duty summonses arrive randomly from voter rolls — employers must give time off, though payment details vary by province.
A bylaw officer left a note about the unshovelled sidewalk.
Bylaws are city-level rules — noise hours, grass height, parking overnight — enforced gently at first, ticketed eventually.
The federal election is on Monday — polls open until eight.
Elections happen at municipal, provincial, and federal levels on separate schedules — permanent residents can vote locally in some municipalities.
City council approved the new bike lanes last night.
City council meetings are public, televised, and surprisingly entertaining — residents can sign up to speak for three minutes.
The public library lends movies, tools, and museum passes too.
A library card is free with ID and unlocks books, streaming, language apps, and free meeting rooms — arguably Canada's best public deal.
As a newcomer, she joined every free walking tour going.
Newcomer is the standard friendly term across settlement services — newcomer centres, newcomer youth programs, welcome guides all use it.
They fired up the barbecue the first sunny weekend of May.
Barbecue doubles as noun and verb, guests bring salads while the host grills burgers, and propane-tank exchanges happen at grocery stores.

translations.hi: प्लेडेट (बच्चों की साथ खेलने की मुलाक़ात)

example_sentences: Can Zoe come over for a playdate on Saturday afternoon?
Playdates are scheduled kid hangouts arranged by parents — hosting means snacks, and dropping off usually means staying the first time.
The street closes for a block party every Victoria Day weekend.
Block parties need a city permit to close the street — neighbours grill, kids chalk the asphalt, and everyone finally learns each other's names.
The whole office watched the hockey game last night.
Hockey defaults to ice hockey in Canada — saying hockey scores is small talk currency from October to June, playoffs especially.
The outdoor rink behind the school froze solid last week.
Neighbourhood outdoor rinks are maintained by volunteers flooding the pad at night — skating there is free, unlike arena ice times.
We rented a canoe at the park and paddled around the lake.
The canoe is practically national symbolism — lakeside towns rent them by the hour, and portaging between lakes is a badge of summer camp honour.
Provincial campsites allow a campfire until eleven at night.
Campfires need permits or designated pits in fire season — check the posted fire rating before lighting anything at the lake.

translations.pa: ਝੀਲ ਕੰਢੇ ਦੀ ਛੁੱਟੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਕੁਟੀਰ
translations.hi: कॉटेज (झील किनारे की छुट्टी की झोपड़ी)

example_sentences: They spend every August long weekend at the cottage.
Cottaging is Ontario shorthand for escaping to lake country — Manitobans say cabin, Quebeckers say chalet, everyone means the same bliss.
Excuse me, where is the washroom in this mall?
Washroom is the polite Canadian word where Americans say restroom and Britons say toilet — signage will say WASHROOM almost everywhere.
